sampling_model.design: Two independent samples from one population: \(\mathcal L_n\sim P^{\otimes n}\) and \(\mathcal U_m\sim P_{XA}^{\otimes m}\).
sampling_model.units: \(n\ge1\) labeled records and \(m\ge0\) outcome-unlabeled records with \(X\in[d]\).
sampling_model.overlap: The fixed known constant satisfies \(0<\epsilon<1/2\); no minimum \(p_x\) is imposed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Neither \(p_x\), \(e_x\), nor \(\mu_{ax}\) is known. The estimator handle uses labeled outcome marks and pooled treatment--mass factorial moments with separate information budgets.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 2 gives the supervised lower scale \(n^{-1}+d^2/(n^2\log^2 n)\) in its stated regime \(d\lesssim n\log n\), and Theorem 5 shows that knowing \(P_X\) alone can leave constant minimax risk.
The paper gives robust and locally efficient semi-supervised ATE estimation using a small chart-reviewed sample and a much larger EHR cohort.
Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.1 give an asymptotic expansion and root-\(n\) normality under explicit nuisance-error controls in the labeled--unlabeled experiment.
The two-sample results derive regular efficient influence functions and an attaining asymptotically normal estimator under support and nuisance-rate conditions.
The paper constructs minimax estimators by applying factorial-moment polynomial estimation on rare cells and a bias-corrected plug-in rule on regular cells.
Theorem 1 matches entropy upper and lower rates through best polynomial approximation and its moment-matching dual.

body.tldr:
The accepted supervised result \(\texttt{stat\_discrete\_ate\_minimax\_loggap\_polynomial\_upper\_match/thm:sharp-minimax-fixed-interior}\) already proves the \(m=0\) two-sided rate in its stated fixed-interior regime; this note's new claim is the unequal-information frontier, in which outcome-bearing moments have \(n\) observations and treatment--mass moments have \(n+m\).  With \(n\) chart-reviewed outcomes and \(m\) additional treatment--covariate records, the unrestricted discrete ATE has minimax mean squared error
\[
 R_\epsilon(n,m,d)\asymp_\epsilon
 \min\!\left\{1,\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{(n+m)^2\log^2(en)}\right\}.
\]
The theorem also supplies its stated all-\((n,m,d)\) extension.  The attaining estimator is a completely specified finite algorithm: it uses the numerical Chebyshev moment constant \(A_\star=7056\), a dyadic lower certificate for overlap, exact deterministic split ratios, and a finite calibration predicate, reverting to zero only on a uniformly finite set of labeled sample sizes.  Its light branch uses one labeled outcome factor per polynomial monomial and obtains all remaining treatment--mass factors from the pooled records.  The common-marginal converse keeps the full random \(P_{XA}\) table identically distributed while changing conditional outcome marks, and therefore retains the \(n^{-1}\) label floor.

project_justification.gap: The accepted supervised result \(\texttt{stat\_discrete\_ate\_minimax\_loggap\_polynomial\_upper\_match/thm:sharp-minimax-fixed-interior}\) proves the \(m=0\) two-sided rate for sufficiently large \(n\) in its stated fixed-interior range \(d\le\rho_\epsilon n\log n\); it does not determine the unequal-information experiment in which outcome-bearing moments have \(n\) observations but treatment--mass moments have \(n+m\).  Regular semi-supervised causal theory instead uses nuisance consistency, working models, or fixed-complexity conditions.  Neither supplies this finite-sample unequal-information frontier with null cells and unrestricted outcome regressions, together with an evaluable estimator calibration.
project_justification.niche: The new object is the annotation frontier separating \(n\)-sample outcome information from \(n+m\)-sample treatment--mass information, with the theorem's stated all-regime extension beyond the accepted result's fixed-interior \(m=0\) regime.  Its upper proof must control false-light polynomial tails and random branch means by mass-weighted sums, without a hidden dimension factor or \(m/n\) leakage.  Its lower proof must preserve the entire random treatment--covariate law, rather than use a supervised prior detectable by the auxiliary sample.
project_justification.fill: The note supplies the matched unequal-information rate \(\min\{1,n^{-1}+[d/\{(n+m)\log(en)\}]^2\}\), an explicitly calibrated and finitely decidable derandomized hybrid estimator, and a normalized common-marginal fuzzy converse.  It positions the accepted result \(\texttt{stat\_discrete\_ate\_minimax\_loggap\_polynomial\_upper\_match/thm:sharp-minimax-fixed-interior}\) as the proved \(m=0\) fixed-interior benchmark, rather than as the new claim.  The calibration fixes \(A_\star=7056\), \(c^\circ=1/256\), computes a dyadic overlap certificate and the least integer \(H_\epsilon\) passing stated scalar inequalities, and tests all moment and tail requirements from \((n,m,\epsilon)\).  The note also retains the inverse-count baseline, the binary-alphabet parametric rate, the exact fixed-\((n,d)\) known-marginal limit, and necessary-and-sufficient growth conditions.

body.related_work: The accepted result \(\texttt{stat\_discrete\_ate\_minimax\_loggap\_polynomial\_upper\_match/thm:sharp-minimax-fixed-interior}\) proves the supervised \(m=0\) two-sided rate for fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), sufficiently large \(n\), and its stated range \(d\le\rho_\epsilon n\log n\). Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy, \cite{ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024}, analyze the same supervised high-dimensional discrete-ATE obstruction; their observable class agrees with the present class modulo irrelevant null-cell propensities. Cheng, Ananthakrishnan, and Cai, \cite{ChengAnanthakrishnanCai2021}, Sections 2.1 and 4, motivate random chart-review labeling and give robust locally efficient semi-supervised procedures using additional structure and outcome surrogates. Chakrabortty and Dai, \cite{ChakraborttyDai2024}, and Kato, \cite{Kato2025}, give adjacent regular asymptotic theories under nuisance-rate conditions. Jiao, Venkat, Han, and Weissman, \cite{JiaoVenkatHanWeissman2015}, and Wu and Yang, \cite{WuYang2016}, provide the classical polynomial-estimation context. The new contribution is the unequal-information \(n\)-versus-\(n+m\) frontier (and this theorem's stated all-regime extension), including the unequal-sample factorial lift, mass-weighted false-branch analysis, and normalized prior whose full random \(P_{XA}\) law agrees exactly. The \(m=0\) formula is the named accepted benchmark, not the new contribution.
body.interpretation: Consistency is equivalent to \(d=o\{(n+m)\log(en)\}\), while parametric mean squared error is equivalent to \(d=O\{(n+m)\log(en)/\sqrt n\}\).  Additional treatment--covariate records improve the minimax order precisely when the supervised rare-cell term dominates \(n^{-1}\) and the corresponding pooled term is asymptotically smaller.  The auxiliary sample changes the approximation term but cannot improve the outcome-information floor.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The estimator is completely evaluable but deliberately conservative: its fixed numerical coefficient bound and finite acceptance predicate are proof certificates, not a claim of computational optimality.  The risk constant remains existential and depends only on the fixed overlap level \(\epsilon\); predicate failure occurs only for finitely many \(n\), uniformly in \(m\), and is absorbed into that constant.  The fixed-\((n,d)\) limit is an equality of minimax risks, whereas the uniform finite-sample theorem determines their common order up to \(\epsilon\)-dependent constants.  No result is asserted for selected enrollment, covariate shift, post-treatment surrogates, continuous covariates, or overlap failure.
body.honest_scope: The result applies to independent random outcome labeling from one shared population, binary treatment and outcome, a known finite covariate alphabet, occupied-cell overlap, and otherwise unrestricted cell masses, propensities, and outcome regressions.  It gives a baseline-only chart-review allocation benchmark for the Cheng--Ananthakrishnan--Cai setting.  It neither claims their surrogate-based efficiency gain nor asserts that their empirical data obey this unrestricted discrete model.
